question: What is the difference between Cosine Distance, Euclidean ($L2$) Distance, and Dot Product?
category: What is the difference between Cosine Distance, Euclidean ($L2$) Distance, and Dot Product?

options.text: Cosine measures angle regardless of magnitude; Euclidean measures geometric distance; Dot product combines angle and magnitude.
It organizes vectors into multi-layer skip-list graphs; upper layers perform long-distance routing; bottom layers perform fine-grained local search.
Flat compares query against every vector ($O(N)$); ANN traverses graph or clusters in sub-linear time ($O(\log N)$) with slight recall trade-off.
The size of the dynamic priority queue during search: higher efsearch yields higher accuracy (recall) at the cost of latency.

explanation: Cosine measures angle regardless of magnitude; Euclidean measures geometric distance; Dot product combines angle and magnitude.
